terrains.name: Grassland
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous open warm olive and sage-green grassland, expressed with three to six broad clusters of short grass hatching per notional world square and restrained pale seed-head marks. No trees, rocks, paths, water, clearings, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Lush green grasses of at least three distinct species grow together in dense, living midsummer growth.

terrains.name: Forest
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous closed forest canopy, expressed with three to six broad overlapping deep teal canopy masses per notional world square, restrained moss-green highlights, and small glimpses of iron-brown forest floor. No clearing, path, water, mountain, or landmark.
terrains.description: Dense trees provide shade and cover.

terrains.name: Mountain
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous warm iron-brown and grey rocky ground, expressed purely as flat two-dimensional cartographic ink hatching — clustered angular line-and-dash marks representing rock texture, never small illustrated peak icons or triangular mountain shapes. Each mark is a flat ink line with no shading, no gradient, and no light or dark side of its own — four to seven broad clustered marks per notional world square, at a raised ink density and wider value-contrast band than grassland's calm baseline, achieved through more ink, not through dimensional form. This must read as a painted flat surface, not a miniature relief map or a drawing of individual mountains. No relief shading, elevation gradient, embossed or 3D-looking marks, summit, snow, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Rocky peaks reach toward the sky.

terrains.name: Mountain Peak
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous cool pale slate-grey sheer summit rock ground with frost-white mineral ink dabs, expressed with five to eight broad tightly clustered fracture-line ink formations per notional world square, at the highest ink density and contrast band in the alpine group. No relief shading, elevation gradient, snowcap gradient, drop shadow, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Jagged summits rise above the clouds, too steep to climb.

terrains.name: Ocean
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous deep desaturated teal-blue open-ocean water, expressed with two to four broad rolling swell-stroke clusters per notional world square and sparse pale foam-crest dashes. The painted surface must fill the canvas completely edge-to-edge with no border, frame, vignette, paper edge, or edge darkening of any kind — the water texture continues unbroken all the way to every edge of the image. No coastline, land, ships, rocks, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Deep ocean waters, impossible to swim across.
terrains.marinerMessage: Swimming through ocean waters with Mariner training!

terrains.name: Deep Water
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous near-black slate-blue deep-water ground, expressed with two to three broad widely spaced long swell-stroke marks per notional world square and minimal dark value variation. This is a flat colour-field swatch, not a framed painting or photograph — there must be no border, frame, vignette, aged-paper edge, deckle edge, or any ring of different colour or darkness around the perimeter. The exact same deep-water colour and texture must reach all four edges and all four corners with zero exception, as if the visible canvas is a cropped sample cut from the middle of a much larger continuous painted surface. No coastline, land, ships, rocks, foam, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Deep water blocks your path.
terrains.marinerMessage: Swimming through deep water with Mariner training!

terrains.name: Sanctuary
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a small roadside waystation shelter — a simple wood-and-stone lean-to with a modest hearth-ring and bench — set on a small cleared patch of open ground. No people, animals, other structures, roads, or water.
terrains.description: A peaceful sanctuary where weary travelers can rest safely.

terrains.name: Shallow Water
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous pale desaturated teal-blue shallow-water ground, expressed with three to five broad short current-ripple ink stroke clusters per notional world square and sparse small wave-crest dash accents. No coastline, land, rocks, paths, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Shallow water that can be waded through.

terrains.name: Beach
terrains.description: Sandy coastline where land meets sea.

terrains.name: Road
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a well-worn packed-earth trail crossing the tile, edges softened with trampled grass and faint wheel-rut ink lines. No travelers, wagons, buildings, bridges, or water.
terrains.description: A well-worn path that connects settlements.

terrains.name: Bridge
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a sturdy wood-and-stone bridge deck spanning a narrow flat strip of calm water, plank or stone-slab surface with visible support-post accents at each edge, set within flat level ground on both banks. The painted surface must fill the canvas completely edge-to-edge with no border, frame, vignette, paper edge, or edge darkening of any kind — the field texture on both banks must continue unbroken all the way to every edge of the image. No canyon, cliffs, ravine, elevation change, relief shading, or dramatic terrain — the banks are flat and unremarkable, not a scenic valley. No travelers, wagons, boats, additional structures, or converging rivers.
terrains.description: A sturdy bridge spans the water.

terrains.name: Town
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a dense cluster of medieval stone-and-timber rooftops along narrow winding streets, roof materials varied between thatch and slate. No people, animals, banners, roads leading off the tile, or water.
terrains.description: A settlement with buildings and people.

terrains.name: Hills
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous uneven sage-olive-brown grass-and-scrub upland ground, expressed with three to six broad clustered tussock and low scrub-brush ink dabs per notional world square and sparse dry pale grass-blade accents. No cliffs, ridgelines, elevation shading, contour lines, rocks, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Rolling hills provide vantage points.

terrains.name: Desert Hills
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous warm rust-ochre ground, deeper in hue than desert, expressed purely as flat two-dimensional cartographic ink hatching — short clustered angular dab-and-dash marks representing broken, eroded rock texture, never a drawn ridge, never a continuous ridgeline, never a landform silhouette. Each mark is a flat ink line with no shading, no gradient, and no light or dark side of its own — four to six broad clustered mark-formations per notional world square, warmer and rounder in silhouette than mountain's hatching, at a raised ink density below full alpine intensity, achieved through more ink marks, not through dimensional form. This must read as a flat painted surface texture, exactly like a hatched fabric pattern, absolutely not a topographic map, not a satellite view, and not a drawing of hills or a mountain range — there must be no continuous line that could be read as a ridge crest, valley, or drainage channel anywhere in the image. No cliffs, elevation shading, contour lines, rock piles, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Eroded sandstone ridges bake under the sun.

terrains.name: Swamp
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous murky desaturated olive-brown wetland ground, expressed with three to six broad dark stagnant-water-pool ink patches per notional world square and sparse reed-and-rush tuft clusters. No open river, clear water, paths, trees, or landmarks.
terrains.description: A murky wetland filled with thick vegetation.

terrains.name: Desert
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous strongly warm golden ochre-cream sand terrain — never grey, never taupe, never desaturated — painted as a flat even colour wash. Expressed with three to six small thin wind-ripple ink line clusters per notional world square, drawn as flat two-dimensional line marks only, plus sparse small dune-crest dash accents drawn as flat ink marks. The surface must read as perfectly flat with no dune ridges, no rolling bands, no directional highlight or shadow, and no sense of height or depth — a flat painted colour field with fine linework texture only, not a landscape. No rocks, oases, water, paths, vegetation, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Endless sands stretch in all directions.

terrains.name: Cave Entrance
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a rocky outcrop with a single dark cave opening at its centre, bare stone surface with sparse scrub growth at the edges. No light source, glow, bones, carvings, treasure, or creatures — the opening reads as a plain unlit gap in the rock, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: A dark opening leading underground.

terrains.name: Ruins
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of weathered stone wall fragments and a broken foundation outline scattered with rubble. One small wall fragment carries a single riftborn material-impossibility accent — stone showing the sharp fracture pattern of shattered glass in one patch that flows smoothly into unbroken, liquid-poured continuity in the next, confined to that one fragment. No visible entrance stairway, glow, carvings, bones, or creatures elsewhere in the frame — the ruin reads as simply old, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: Ancient structures crumbling with age.

terrains.name: Temple
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a single small wayside stone shrine — drawn strictly as a flat architectural roof plan seen from vertically above, exactly as a floor plan is drawn: the building is one solid pale flat quadrilateral of stone roof lying flat on the ground plane, its four edges square to the viewer, with a row of small round column tops reading as a line of pale dots along one edge and one small darker altar rectangle set just beside them. Every surface lies flat in the picture plane; the walls are hidden beneath the roof and no side face, gable end, elevation, or cast shadow is visible anywhere. The building spans roughly two fifths of the tile width, centred, and is the clear subject — large enough to read as a solid pale rectangle when the image is reduced to 32 pixels. A few small plain stone and metal votive tokens rest on the slab, unremarkable and non-luminous. One structure only: no additional buildings, outbuildings, hamlet, village, enclosing walls, or second shrine anywhere in the frame. The surrounding ground is flat muted olive-green open sward, quiet and much lower in detail than the building, carrying the same even painted grass texture and the same tone at the centre, at all four edges, and in all four corners alike. The image is a swatch cropped from the middle of a much larger continuous painted field: the grass runs off all four sides mid-stroke, and the outermost pixels are ordinary grass identical to the middle. No trees, no canopy, no scrub, no roads, no water. At thumbnail size this must read as one solid pale rectangle sitting on a mid-toned green field. Every shape in the tile lies flat in the picture plane, as on a surveyor's plan. No glass, no glazing, no domes, spheres, or orbs, no crystal, no reflective or iridescent surfaces, and no anomalous or out-of-place objects anywhere in the frame. No glow, worshippers, clergy, incense, candles, flowers, banners, dark stains, bones, or creatures — the shrine reads as simply old and quiet, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: A modest shrine of carved stone, incense lingering in the air.

terrains.name: Monastery
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a single walled discipline house — plain slate-grey stone hall roofs forming one closed rectangular ring around an open empty pale gravel inner courtyard, so the whole structure reads as a hollow rectangle with a light open centre. The ring spans roughly three fifths of the tile width, leaving a clear margin of open ground on all four sides — it must not fill or nearly fill the frame. One ring only: a single wall line, never nested, concentric, or repeated rectangles inside one another. Along one outer side sit a few narrow stepped terrace planting beds, uniform and without ornament, painted as flat stacked bands with no shading, no shadow, and no suggestion of height. One structure only: no additional buildings, outbuildings, hamlet, village, or second courtyard anywhere in the frame. The surrounding ground is flat pale cold grey stony open ground with sparse dark lichen flecks, quiet and much lower in detail than the structure, filling the tile to every edge — no trees, no roads, no water. No spire, steeple, bell tower, bell, cross, statue, altar, carved symbol, or religious iconography of any kind: this is a secular working house of austere self-sufficiency, not a place of worship. No cliff, ravine, gorge, escarpment, drop-off, elevation gradient, relief shading, hillshade, embossing, or cast shadow implying height — the ground reads flat. Rendered directly overhead and flat, never at an angle or isometric perspective. No glass, no glazing, no domes, spheres, or orbs, no crystal, no reflective or iridescent surfaces, and no anomalous or out-of-place objects anywhere in the frame. No glow, monks, people, banners, or creatures — the structure reads as simply a plain walled house, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: A cloistered retreat of quiet stone halls and terraced gardens.

terrains.name: Camp
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a very sparse small camp on open ground: two weathered canvas tents, one cold ash-grey firepit ring, and one or two plain wooden supply crates, every one of them drawn strictly as a flat plan seen from vertically above. Each tent is a flat elongated hexagonal canvas shape lying flat on the ground plane, divided down its long axis by one straight ridge line into two equal flat panels, with four short guy-rope lines running out to small stake dots — the shape of a tent as traced on a floor plan, lying entirely in the picture plane. Each crate is one small flat square. The firepit is one small flat dark circle. No more than five painted marks in total across the entire tile — each mark large, widely separated, with open ground between them. This is the sparsest tile in the set and must not be filled in. A single small camp only: no buildings, outbuildings, hamlet, village, palisade, wagons, or second camp anywhere in the frame. The surrounding ground is flat bare dust-tan trodden earth, quiet and much lower in detail than the tents, carrying the same even painted earth texture and the same tone at the centre, at all four edges, and in all four corners alike. The image is a swatch cropped from the middle of a much larger continuous painted field: the ground runs off all four sides mid-stroke, and the outermost pixels are ordinary trodden earth identical to the middle. No trees, no crops, no roads, no water. At thumbnail size this must read as a few small scattered marks on an open field, never as one solid mass. The canvas is plain and weathered, pitched over a straight ridge pole. Every shape in the tile lies flat in the picture plane, as on a surveyor's plan. No visible flame, smoke, banners, bones, or people — the camp reads as simply unoccupied, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: A cluster of weathered tents and cold firepits, abandoned or not-quite-abandoned.

terrains.name: Watchtower
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a single small round fortified stone tower standing alone on open ground, weathered but structurally intact. Seen from directly above the tower is one small hard-edged ring of cool grey stone with an evenly notched crenellated rim; the rooftop enclosed inside the ring is pale stone floor and reads light — never a dark opening, shaft, hole, or void. The tower is the clear subject of the tile: its ring spans roughly one third of the tile width, centred, large enough to stay legible when the image is reduced to 32 pixels — never a small distant dot in a wide empty field. One structure only: no courtyard, no attached wall, no palisade, no outbuildings, no second tower, and no hamlet or village anywhere in the frame. The surrounding ground is flat muted olive-brown upland grass, quiet and much lower in detail than the tower, filling the tile to every edge — no trees, no roads, no water. No cliff, ravine, gorge, escarpment, drop-off, elevation gradient, relief shading, hillshade, embossing, or cast shadow implying height — the ground reads flat. Rendered directly overhead and flat, never at an angle or isometric perspective. No glass, no glazing, no domes, spheres, or orbs, no crystal, no reflective or iridescent surfaces, and no anomalous or out-of-place objects anywhere in the frame. No banners, guards, fire, glow, or creatures — the tower reads as simply a fortified structure, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: A fortified tower standing watch over the surrounding land.

terrains.name: Villa
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a single modest countryside villa on open ground, composed as two clearly unequal zones: a solid warm terracotta-red tiled roof mass occupying one side of the tile, and beside it — not surrounding it — one bounded rectangular patch of broad, regular, deep-green ornamental garden beds inside a low stone wall. The two zones are deliberately asymmetric and different in colour, so the tile reads at thumbnail size as one warm red mass with a darker green patch set off to one side. Garden beds are broad and generously spaced, painted as loose hand-brushed rows with natural irregularity, never mechanically ruled or grid-aligned. One structure only: no additional buildings, outbuildings, cottages, hamlet, village, or second courtyard anywhere in the frame. The surrounding ground is flat pale straw-gold open grass, quiet and much lower in detail than the villa, filling the tile to every edge — no trees, no crop fields, no roads, no water. Rendered directly overhead and flat, never at an angle or isometric perspective. No glass, no glazing, no domes, spheres, or orbs, no crystal, no reflective or iridescent surfaces, and no anomalous or out-of-place objects anywhere in the frame. No people, banners, glow, or creatures — the estate reads as simply a rural dwelling, not clearly safe or clearly dangerous.
terrains.description: A sprawling countryside estate behind low garden walls.

terrains.name: Plains
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous wide open dry golden-straw grassland ground, expressed with three to six broad sweeping tall-grass-blade brushstroke clusters per notional world square and sparse small pale flower-dot accents. No trees, rocks, paths, water, clearings, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Wide open lowland, green and alive in full growth, grasses dense and knee-high under a clear sky.

terrains.name: Dense Forest
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous closed dense-forest canopy in cooler near-black teal than open forest. Canopy clusters must touch and overlap edge-to-edge with almost no gaps between them, so the pale ground substrate is barely visible anywhere in the image — this is a noticeably denser, more closed canopy than a normal forest, not a scattering of separated tree clumps with visible ground between them. Expressed with four to seven broad tightly overlapping canopy-mass ink clusters per notional world square, at a contrast band one step above forest's baseline. No clearing, path, water, mountain, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Thick forest with towering trees and dense undergrowth.

terrains.name: Tundra
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous pale cool blue-grey frozen ground, expressed with three to six broad sparse low scrub-tuft ink dab clusters per notional world square and small dark exposed-ground stipple patches. No snow drifts, ice, rocks, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Frozen ground with sparse vegetation.

terrains.name: Snowy Plains
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous flat pale blue-white snow-covered ground, painted as an even flat colour wash over a visible warm stone-grey substrate. Expressed with three to six small soft pale brushstroke dashes per notional world square, scattered evenly across the surface as flat two-dimensional marks, plus sparse small dark exposed-scrub or stone accent dabs for value anchoring. The surface must read as perfectly flat with no ridges, no drifts, no dunes, no directional highlight or shadow, and no sense of height or depth — a flat painted colour field with light surface texture only, not a landscape. No trees, mountains, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Snow-covered plains glitter in the cold.

terrains.name: Jungle
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous dense tropical-jungle canopy in deep saturated humid green, the most saturated hue in the terrain set. Canopy-mass clusters must touch and overlap edge-to-edge with almost no gaps between them, so the ground substrate is barely visible anywhere in the image — this must read as the single densest, most fully covered canopy in the whole terrain set, denser than denseForest. Expressed with five to eight broad densely overlapping broad-leaf canopy-mass ink clusters per notional world square and trailing vine-stroke accents filling any remaining small gaps, at the highest ink density and contrast band in its terrain group. This is a flat colour-field swatch, not a framed painting — there must be no border, frame, vignette, or aged-paper edge of any kind; canopy clusters must reach and touch all four edges and all four corners with zero exception, as if the visible canvas is a cropped sample cut from the middle of a much larger continuous canopy. No clearing, path, water, mountain, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Dense tropical jungle teeming with life.

terrains.name: Savanna
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous warm dry gold savanna ground, expressed with four to six broad flat-topped canopy-blob ink clusters per notional world square and sparse dry tall-grass dash accents, at a contrast band raised above plains' baseline. Each canopy-blob is a flat top-down silhouette shape only, viewed directly from above, matching the same flat orthographic motif language as grassland and forest's canopy marks — no visible trunks, no branch structure, no side-on or three-quarter view of any tree, and no illustrated individual trees. No dense forest, rocks, paths, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Warm-climate grassland, green and dry-season sparse, scattered with flat-topped trees under a high bright sun.

terrains.name: Residential
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a closely clustered residential quarter of modest timber-and-thatch house rooftops lining narrow lanes, matching the same illustrative rooftop-and-street cartographic style as a town centre but smaller in scale and lower in density. More houses than open ground — only occasional small garden patches, never broad cultivated fields or crop rows; this must read as a housing quarter, not farmland. No people, animals, shop signage, roads leading off the tile, or water.
terrains.description: Houses and shops line the streets of the settlement outskirts.

terrains.name: Farmland
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous warm golden-brown cultivated farmland ground, entirely dry earth-tone in colour with no blue or teal anywhere in the image. Expressed with three to six broad evenly spaced furrow-row and planted-field patch motifs per notional world square, rendered as loose hand-painted brushstrokes with irregular natural variation — never mechanically ruled or grid-straight. No ponds, puddles, irrigation ditches, wet ground, or any water of any kind. No structures, people, animals, paths, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Cultivated fields and pastures surround the settlement.

terrains.name: Industrial
terrains.imageDescription: Directly overhead view of a cluster of stone-and-timber workshop and warehouse rooftops with small forge-chimney smoke-wisp accents, matching the same illustrative rooftop-and-street cartographic style as a town centre, medieval craft-quarter in character. Every rooftop surface is plain worn wood, thatch, or stone tile only — no glass, no glazing, no glass domes or spheres, no orbs, no reflective or iridescent surfaces, no crystal, and no anomalous or out-of-place objects anywhere on any rooftop. Rendered directly overhead and flat, never at an angle or isometric perspective. No modern machinery, no glowing light, no electricity, no magical effects or energy, no people, roads leading off the tile, or water.
terrains.description: Warehouses, workshops, and forges bustle with activity.

terrains.name: Dungeon Floor
terrains.description: Cold stone floor stretches into darkness.

terrains.name: Dungeon Wall
terrains.description: Solid stone wall blocks your path.

terrains.name: Door
terrains.description: A wooden door leading to another chamber.

terrains.name: Dungeon Exit
terrains.description: Stairs leading back to the surface.

terrains.name: Underground Pool
terrains.description: Dark water fills this section of the dungeon.

terrains.name: Pit
terrains.description: A gaping pit drops into darkness below.

terrains.name: Rubble
terrains.description: Broken stones and debris litter the floor.

terrains.name: Altar
terrains.description: An ancient altar stands here, dark stains marking its surface.

terrains.name: Treasure Chest
terrains.description: A treasure chest sits here, waiting to be opened.

terrains.name: Trapped Floor
terrains.description: The floor here looks suspicious...

terrains.name: Spider Web
terrains.description: Thick webs cling to everything here.

terrains.name: Lava
terrains.description: Molten rock glows with deadly heat.

terrains.name: Ice Floor
terrains.description: Slippery ice covers the floor.

terrains.name: Mushroom Grove
terrains.description: Giant glowing mushrooms illuminate the cavern.

terrains.name: Bone Pile
terrains.description: Scattered calcified remains and dungeon detritus cover the stone floor.

terrains.name: Snow Forest
terrains.imageDescription: Continuous closed conifer-forest canopy in cold slate-teal-green, expressed with four to seven broad overlapping canopy-mass ink clusters per notional world square and pale snow-load edge-dab accents along each canopy silhouette, at a medium-high contrast band. No clearing, path, open ground, water, or landmarks.
terrains.description: Dense conifer forest draped in snow. Wind whispers through dark boughs.
